related_resources.reason: Interior H-two regularity theorem and difference quotient proof.

authorship.scope: New original narration and mathematical companions explaining elliptic boundary traces, Neumann/Robin conditions, difference quotient regularity, and corner singularity effects on finite-element error; earlier manuscripts unchanged.

prerequisites.reason: Existence of an H-one weak solution and the meaning of weak derivative.
Which boundary hypotheses do and do not follow from trace theory.
Why H-two smoothness matters for finite-element interpolation error.

recommended.reason: Examine a reentrant corner where global H-two regularity fails.
Connect Fourier multipliers with rough derivatives.

background: Distributional derivatives in an elementary sense, Cauchy–Schwarz and Young inequalities, introductory Fourier modes, and the weak Poisson problem.
readiness_checks: Verify the piecewise Poisson solution with a discontinuous load belongs to H-two but not C-two.
State the coefficient and interior-domain assumptions in the H-two difference quotient estimate.
